You're looking forward to unveiling your new setup to your family and friends.When the delivery finally arrived at my door, I noticed the outer box had seven crushed corners, which made me a bit uneasy. The top was slightly caved in, like something heavy had been stacked on it in the truck. Now, I understand that sometimes boxes can look a little rough in transit, and the product inside can still be fine—that's how shipping goes. But as soon as I peeled back the tape, I could see a bigger problem: part of the espresso machine's stainless-steel body on the right side is scuffed and actually dented inward. It's not just a faint scratch or something cosmetic; it's a significant dent that also left a few sharp edges. It's almost like the machine was hit from the side with something.I decided to carefully pull the entire unit out of the box and check the rest of it. The drip tray had popped out of place(no big deal, I figured I could snap it back in), but it looks like the steam wand is also bent at an odd angle—definitely not the sleek shape it's supposed to have. I tried gently moving it to see if maybe it was just jammed, but it doesn't swivel smoothly, and I'm worried if I try to straighten it, something inside might snap. Honestly, this was so disappointing to see, especially after all the anticipation and the back-and-forth we had in trying to get shipping sorted.To be thorough, I also took a look at the accessories I ordered—the stainless-steel frothing pitcher and some extra filters. The pitcher came in a separate smaller box within the main package and seems to be okay, with just a tiny scratch on the outside. I can live with that if necessary(though I’m sure it’d be nice to have it in perfect condition), but the bigger issue is definitely the main espresso unit. I haven’t even tried plugging it in yet because I’m worried the damage might cause an electrical issue or leak water if anything inside got cracked. There’s a water reservoir area that I can see is slightly misaligned, and the hinge doesn’t close flush. That’s really concerning.I figured the best course of action was to reach out to you immediately rather than attempt to use the machine. For one, I don’t want to do anything that might void whatever warranty or guarantee came with it. And for another, I’d rather be safe than sorry—I paid a decent amount for this, plus I was so excited to finally upgrade my coffee experience. It would be a bummer to start off with a compromised machine and then deal with bigger problems down the road.In terms of the timing, I was hoping to have this all resolved quickly because, as I mentioned before, I do a fair amount of hosting—especially casual weekend gatherings. My siblings and close friends have been asking non-stop if I’ve finally brewed any cappuccinos or lattes yet. It’s kind of ironic that after all this build-up, I’m left explaining that the machine arrived in less-than-ideal shape. I mean, we’re still making do with my backup French press, but it’s just not the same as those café-style espresso drinks that I was hoping to serve.I’m really hoping we can figure out a replacement process that’s hassle-free. To be honest, I had some unpleasant experiences in the past with other companies where they made me jump through hoops—like sending multiple photos, filling out complicated forms, waiting for a shipping label to arrive by snail mail, and so on. I’d like to avoid that if possible. Of course, I’m happy to provide proof of the damage. I actually took a bunch of photos right after I unboxed everything: I’ve got shots of the exterior of the box showing where it was crushed, plus close-ups of the dents on the stainless-steel panel and the bent steam wand. If you need a video, I can record one as well; I’m pretty tech-savvy, so just tell me how you’d prefer me to send them.
